title: Personal data and sensitive data: what changes in how you handle it

videos.script: A pharmacy's order lines have five columns. An order, a line, a product, a quantity, a price. Nothing in them looks like a medical record. {{lines}} Join the product to its category, and three and a half thousand customers bought a psychiatric medicine. Sixteen hundred bought a pregnancy test. {{inference}} The law does not ask which table data sits in. It asks what the data reveals. {{reveals}} This lesson finds Ipê's personal data, and its sensitive data, column by column. Twenty customers turn out to be adolescents. Support tickets turn out to hold CPFs and medicines nobody asked for. {{finds}} Then every column gets a class, in the database, with a query that fails the day somebody adds one without deciding what it holds. {{classes}} You cannot protect, export or delete what you have not found. Finding it is where governance starts. {{end}}
